title.en: A boy, a puppy and a muddy pit

text.en: Badal lives with his mother in a village. One evening he finds a shivering puppy by the road and brings it home. He names the puppy Moti. When Badal falls into a deep pit on a rainy day, it is Moti who finds him. In this chapter you will read the story, learn how past actions end in ed, learn about questions and statements, and put story events in order.

Badal is a boy who lives with his mother in a village, and they are very happy. One evening, when Badal is coming back from school, he sees a puppy shivering in the cold and brings it home. His mother says the puppy can stay only if Badal promises to take care of it. Badal and his mother name the puppy Moti. Moti grows up and loves Badal. They eat and play together, and Moti follows Badal everywhere.
One rainy day Badal slips on a muddy lane and falls into a deep pit. He tries hard but cannot climb out. When Badal does not come home on time, his mother is worried and gathers the neighbours to search for him. Moti goes with them. Moti catches Badal's scent, follows it to the pit and starts barking. The barking tells the neighbours where Badal is. They pull him out with a rope, and Badal hugs Moti and thanks him. The story shows that a pet who is cared for loves us and can help us when we need it.
The words lived, loved, played, gathered and thanked all end with ed. These words tell us about actions that have already happened. This is called the past. To tell about the past we can often add ed to an action word: walk becomes walked, play becomes played, talk becomes talked, ask becomes asked and touch becomes touched.
A sentence that asks something is a question, and it ends with a question mark (?). A sentence that tells something is a statement, and it ends with a full stop (.). Can this puppy stay with us? is a question. The sun rises in the east is a statement. Every sentence begins with a capital letter.
A story has a beginning, a middle and an end. Events must be told in the order in which they happened. In this story, Badal first finds the puppy, then names him Moti, then falls in the pit, then Moti barks, and last Badal hugs Moti. Why does Badal's mother start looking for him? Find the clue in what happens before the neighbours leave to search.
Badal usually comes home on time. When he is late, his mother is worried. The story shows that feeling through what she does next.

board.text: Feeling → action: she asks for help

text.en: Moti helps the neighbours find the pit and the neighbours use a rope to bring Badal up. Tell how these two actions work together.
Listen to these two ideas: Today I help at home. Yesterday I helped at home. What changed in the action word?
Help became helped when we talked about yesterday. We can do the same with call and called, or look and looked.
Care already ends in e. When we talk about the past, we add d to make cared. Read both words aloud.
Some past words change in another way. We say Badal falls when we tell what happens now, and Badal fell when we tell what happened before.
Listen to, The gate is open. Now listen to, Is the gate open? One tells us something. Which one asks us for an answer?

board.text: The gate is open. | Is the gate open?

text.en: Is the gate open asks for an answer and gets a question mark. The gate is open tells us something and gets a full stop.
Put three events in order: the neighbours arrive at the pit, Moti finds a scent, and Moti barks. What must happen before the neighbours know where to go?

board.text: Finds a scent → barks → neighbours arrive

text.en: Retell one part of the story using first, then and finally. Ask your listener to repeat the three events so you can check that the order is clear.

commonMisconceptions.en: Moti found Badal by his photo

points.en: Badal finds a puppy and names him Moti.
Moti follows Badal's scent and saves him from the pit.
Past actions often end in ed.
Questions end with ?, statements end with a full stop.
Story events must be in the right order.
